marks.gloss_en: and here the difference between them is [urine] moist enough to moisten
דאמר רבי יוחנן: ותיקין היו גומרין אותה עם הנץ החמה -- the mishnah's 'before sunrise' can be the vatikin's practice
you may even say [the mishnah is] R' Yehoshua's
the mishnah: one who went down to immerse -- if he can come up [cover himself and read before sunrise, he comes up, covers himself and reads]
the mishnah's 'cover himself in water' was taught of turbid water, which is like solid ground, so his heart does not see his nakedness
במים עכורין שנו, דדמו כארעא סמיכתא, שלא יראה לבו ערותו -- it was taught of turbid water, which is like solid ground, so that his heart does not see his nakedness
clear water: he sits in it up to his neck and reads
the heart seeing the nakedness is permitted (the tanna kama's implied position)
the heel touching the nakedness -- forbidden to read
feces behind glass: permitted to read the Shema facing it
a minimal quantity of feces may be nullified with spittle
a naked gentile: forbidden to read the Shema facing him
תא שמע: the second baraita has 'behind the bed -- reads at once; before the bed -- distances four amot', the first reading's pattern
baraita B as recited: R' Shimon ben Elazar -- behind at once, before four amot; RSBG -- even a house of a hundred amot...
R' Shimon ben Elazar is the one who holds the whole house is like four amot, so the hundred-amot ruling is his and the latter baraita is the one to reverse
מאן שמעת ליה דאמר כוליה בית כארבע אמות דמי -- רבי שמעון בן אלעזר היא: the hundred-amot ruling fits R' Shimon ben Elazar, so baraita A's assignment stands
the one heard to say the whole house is like four amot is R' Shimon ben Elazar
שפיר עבדת דלא איבעיא לך, כל עשרה רשותא אחריתי היא -- you did well not to ask: any ten is another domain
a bed less than three [tefachim high]: obvious to me that it is like lavud
דתניא: a house with a Torah scroll or tefillin is forbidden for marital relations until they are taken out or put in a vessel within a vessel
Rav Achai married his son into the house of Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta; the marriage did not succeed; he went to look and saw a Torah scroll lying there
מתנייתא קשיין אהדדי -- baraita A gives the hundred-amot ruling to R' Shimon ben Elazar, baraita B gives it to RSBG
איפוך בתרייתא -- reverse the names in the latter baraita (= p_eipoch_batraita)
the baraitot contradict each other: reverse [the names in] the latter one
מה חזית דאפכת בתרייתא? איפוך קמייתא! -- nothing yet decides which baraita to reverse
a chamber pot for excrement and a urine vessel: forbidden to read the Shema facing them, even if there is nothing in them
reading A of RSBG: behind the bed -- he reads at once; before the bed -- he distances four amot and reads
the halakha follows R' Shimon ben Elazar
Abaye: they taught this only of a vessel that is not their own vessel
how much water must he put into them? any amount
Rav Nachman: the dispute is [in the case] at the end
Rav Yosef: the dispute is [in the case] at the beginning
והרי לבו רואה את הערוה? -- standing in the water with nothing between, his heart sees his nakedness; how can he read?
the mishnah: and if not, he covers himself in the water and reads
וכמה מיא רמי ואזיל? -- read as it stands, the 'until he puts water' clause governs foul and soaking water: how much water would he go on pouring?
אלא הכי קאמר: foul and soaking water not at all; the 'until he puts water' clause is about urine (= p_hachi_kaamar_mei_raglayim)
the mishnah: he may not cover himself with foul water nor with flax-soaking water until he puts water into them
